comments.note: MovieListItem.StoredTagIds and StoredTagParentIds default to empty lists per spec comment ('after effective-set enrichment pass lands in a later WP'). DapperMovieCatalogRepository.GetMovieListAsync does not populate them yet. Downstream consumers relying on these fields in filter expressions (HasTag DSL, TagHasSubTags DSL) will silently get empty results until the enrichment WP ships. This is by design but should be verified in that WP's QA pass.

MovieListItem.EffectiveTagIds default is 'new HashSet<long>()', creating a fresh mutable instance per record. Consider a shared static readonly empty set (e.g. ImmutableHashSet<long>.Empty or a static readonly HashSet) to avoid heap allocation on every row that hasn't been enriched yet.

DapperMovieRepository.GetByIdAsync issues two sequential queries on the same open connection (main SELECT then StoredTagIds SELECT). If the connection is closed between calls or the cancellation token fires between them, the second query will fail mid-operation. Current implementation looks safe since the connection is held open in a using block, but the cancellation token is not threaded to the second QueryAsync call — it uses the Dapper default (none). Recommend passing cancellationToken to the second QueryAsync call for consistency.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: changed MovieListItem.EffectiveTagIds default from 'new HashSet<long>()' to 'ImmutableHashSet<long>.Empty'. Every unenriched row in the movies list was allocating a fresh empty HashSet; the ImmutableHashSet<long>.Empty singleton eliminates the hot-path allocation at no behavioral cost. Added 'using System.Collections.Immutable;' to MovieListItem.cs. Build and 682 tests verified clean.

MoviesListView.axaml Tag Weight column binds to EffectiveTagWeight (will show 0 for all rows until the enrichment WP ships) while the Tag Count column binds to StoredTagCount (populated from SQL immediately). This intentional asymmetry is documented in the Developer handoff but has no in-code comment. Until enrichment lands, users will see 0 in the Tag Weight column. Consider adding an AXAML comment or a TODO noting the placeholder state to prevent confusion during ongoing M7 development.

DapperMovieRepository.GetByIdAsync and all other Dapper query calls across the codebase omit CancellationToken from the SQL execution itself (token is only used at connection-open time). This is a consistent but imperfect pattern: queries cannot be cancelled mid-flight. Recommend a codebase-wide sweep to use CommandDefinition(sql, param, cancellationToken: ct) across all repositories in a dedicated debt-reduction WP.

[documentation-forward] FilterExpressionEvaluator XML remarks list HasTags() as 'StoredTagCount > 0'. After the enrichment WP ships, HasTags() semantics should be reviewed — the natural expectation post-M7 is 'does this movie have any effective tags?' (EffectiveTagCount > 0). Add a TODO comment in FilterExpressionEvaluator noting this pending semantic revision so the Documentation agent can capture it in the M7 release notes.
